FROM A MODEL TO YOUR PLACE

The space is the interface.

This is a working spatial prototype. A connected digital twin needs verified geometry, asset identities and authorised data.

01 / MAP THE PLACE

Your plan, in three dimensions.

Start with an approved floor plan, measurements or IFC model. Name the rooms, bays and equipment. Check scale and access routes with the site team.

Image reference only, kept in this tab. It does not automatically replace the 3D geometry.

02 / MAP THE SIGNALS

Every reading has a home.

Map meters and sensors to an asset: timestamp, unit, source and freshness. Start with read-only readings. Flag missing or stale data visibly.

03 / MAKE IT ACTIONABLE

A human approves the change.

Prepare a maintenance task, service update or operating schedule. A future approved connection can send it to the right system and keep an action record.

Floor-plan reference · not a measured 3D conversion

Visible only in this browser tab. No upload has been sent to a server.

Read the model assumptions, sources and limits

All layouts are original illustrative geometry, not surveys or reproductions of actual premises. The Penrose concept is informed by Winger’s published service offering; its bay count, floor plan, vehicles, schedules and staffing are invented for demonstration. Winger states that its Trade Parts Centre is across the road. No affiliation, endorsement or operational integration is implied.

The workshop uses ten synthetic jobs (thirteen with the extra-bookings option), one 15-minute inspection station, one to three service bays, 45–100 minutes of service and one 10-minute final-check station. Jobs wait off-bay for approval and parts. No staff breaks, skill constraints, walking time or real vehicle data are included. The demo runs from 08:00 to 17:00; this is not Winger’s opening-hours schedule.

Energy is an hourly electrical balance for a made-up day. Displayed kW is the constant power assumed within that hour. Summing those hourly values gives daily kWh. Solar uses a synthetic 06:00–18:00 sine profile with a weather multiplier; it is not an address-specific yield forecast. The optional home battery starts empty, has a 3 kW power limit and 95% efficiency in each direction. The end-of-day energy remains stored. A shifted EV or hot-water load uses the same energy at a different time. No tariffs, payback, thermal comfort, carbon, HVAC design or safety performance are modelled.

School and business zoning changes assumed non-essential loads outside occupied hours. Essential services remain on. It does not demonstrate that occupied spaces can safely reduce ventilation or heating. All power values are illustrative assumptions. Imported CSV readings are snapshots, not a live feed, and do not drive a calibrated forecast.

Sources reviewed 23 October 2026: Winger Penrose services; Ministry of Education: energy monitoring; School property: solar and energy controls; Woolworths shopping policies; Mitre 10 guides. Creative references: April Zhu’s Colorfigures and Airsup’s fab simulation. This implementation uses original Three.js scenes, not those projects’ code or assets.
